newsitem.title: USA: Greenwich to merge with UNC.
newsitem.headline: Greenwich to merge with UNC.

text.p: Greenwich Air Services Inc said Friday it had reached a definitive agreement to merge with UNC Inc in a deal worth no less than $320 million.
The company said it will give UNC sharholders will give at least $14 worth of Greenwich Class B Non-Voting Common Stock for each share of UNC stock held.
If the market price for the Class B stock rose above $24.86 per share, UNC shareholders would receive additional value above $14 per share, up to $16.10 of value for each UNC share held, it said.
The company said it had also offered UNC shareholders the option of receiving cash in lieu of Class B stock up to a maximum of 50 percent of the value of the deal.
The transaction is expected to be completed in the spring of 1997, it added.
The company said UNC would merge into it, bringing Greenwich's annual revenues from commercial aviation engine services and business aviation services to nearly $1.8 billion.

"We believe the new combined company will enjoy significant cost-savings in each of our businesses as well as significant opportunities for revenue growth through new business partnerships," it said. "These savings and benefits, we believe, will allow this transaction to be accretive to our shareholders after fiscal 1997."
Greenwich Air Services, based in Miami, Florida, is a gas turbine engine repair and overhaul company.
UNC, based in Annapolis, Maryland, is an aviation services company.
